{{Short description|Mathematics concept}}
In [[mathematics]], a  [[topological space]] is '''feebly compact''' if every [[locally finite collection|locally finite]] cover by nonempty [[open set]]s is finite. The concept was introduced by [[Sibe Mardešić]] and P. Papić in 1955.<ref name="hattori">{{cite journal |last1=Hattori |first1=Yasunao |title=THE WORK OF PROFESSOR KIYOSHI ISEKI ON TOPOLOGY |journal=Scientiae Mathematicae Japonicae |date=20 May 2013 |volume=76 |issue=2 |url=https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/isms/76/2/76_299/_pdf |access-date=26 September 2022}}</ref>

Some facts:

* Every [[compact space]] is feebly compact.<ref name="hattori" />
* Every feebly compact [[paracompact space]] is [[compact space|compact]].{{citation needed|date=September 2022}}
* Every feebly compact space is [[pseudocompact space|pseudocompact]] but the converse is not necessarily true.<ref name="hattori" />
* For a [[completely regular space|completely regular]] [[Hausdorff space]] the properties of being feebly compact and pseudocompact are equivalent.{{citation needed|date=September 2022}}
* Any maximal feebly compact space is [[submaximal space|submaximal]].<ref name="springer">{{cite book |editor1-last=Hrušák |editor1-first=Michael |editor2-last=Tkachenko |editor2-first=Mikhail |editor3-last=Tamariz-Mascarúa |editor3-first=Ángel |title=Pseudocompact Topological Spaces: A Survey of Classic and New Results with Open Problems |date=19 July 2018 |publisher=Springer International Publishing |page=193 |isbn=978-3-319-91680-4 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=fsRlDwAAQBAJ&dq=Any+maximal+feebly+compact+space+is+submaximal&pg=PA193 |access-date=26 September 2022}}</ref>
